claim: FCI permits latent variables and does not assume the observed set is causally sufficient.
source: Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2000), Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.

claim: Possible-D-SEP is a computable superset defined by collider-or-triangle path triples, and both ordered endpoint searches are required.
source: Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2000), Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.
locator: Chapter 6 §6.7, definition before Fast Causal Inference Algorithm, printed p. 144

claim: The 2000 FCI schedule is adjacency search, initial collider orientation, Possible-D-SEP refinement, reset/reorientation, then orientation closure.

locator: Chapter 6 §6.7, Fast Causal Inference Algorithm, printed pp. 144–145

claim: An unshielded triple A-B-C is oriented as a collider when B is absent from the separating set of A and C.
source: Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2000), Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.
locator: Chapter 6, Causal Inference Algorithm step C, printed p. 139; reused by FCI p. 145

claim: After Possible-D-SEP removals, FCI resets retained endpoints and repeats collider and propagation orientation.
source: Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2000), Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.

claim: Under Faithfulness and correct decisions, original FCI returns a partially oriented inducing-path graph of the observed margin.
source: Spirtes, Glymour, and Scheines (2000), Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.

claim: The 2000 source explicitly leaves maximal informativeness of the original orientation schedule open.

claim: Later orientation rules provide completeness for modern PAG representations under latent confounding and selection bias.

claim: FCI+ defines a sparse causal-learning task with a constant-time exact independence oracle and Faithfulness to an underlying causal DAG.

claim: HIE is a fixed-point union of seed nodes and nodes in recorded minimal separators among pairs already in the hierarchy.

claim: Algorithm 2 consists of bounded PC adjacency search, augmentation, candidate detection, paired endpoint bases, hierarchy testing/minimization, rebuilding, and complete final orientation.
